result.text:
I didn't add an ETA cache, and I couldn't reproduce the slowness in-process, so I changed no handler code. All 88 tests pass.

- **Why no cache:** the ledger records ETA caching as a dead end. QA found a memoized version serving stale ETAs after a new event such as an exception, because it wasn't invalidated.
- **Why the premise doesn't hold:** `GET /shipments` already cuts the list to `limit` before computing ETAs. The default is 50 and the maximum is 500, so `calculateEta` runs for at most 500 shipments, not 5k.
- **Measured with 5k shipments:**

  | `limit` | List and sort | ETA calculation |
  |---|---|---|
  | 50 (default) | 0.6 ms | 0.2 ms |
  | 500 | 0.1 ms | 1.6 ms |
  | 5000 | 0.2 ms | 14 ms |

- **Likely cause on staging:** if it's really slow there, the cause is probably outside this code, such as store file I/O, the bind mount, network or response size. I'd profile on staging itself. I can add timing logs for it if you want. Pagination, which the ledger already plans, would help if clients request large limits.
- **New test:** `test/list-perf.test.ts` loads 5k shipments and checks three things:
  - The list returns exactly `limit` items.
  - A 500-item request finishes in under 500 ms.
  - The ETA changes immediately after a new exception event. This is the check that would catch a stale cache.

I also added the measurements and the decision to `.gemkeeper/ledger.md`.

# Ledger: parcel-tracker
<!-- gemkeeper ledger. Written for the next session. Keep it under ~120 lines. Edit in place. -->
Updated: 2026-11-17

## Mission
- Work on parcel-tracker (shipment tracking service, Vienna warehouse; Node 24 runs TS directly, no build step, zero deps). Task 1: calculateEta (src/services/eta.ts) must skip Austrian public holidays, not just weekends; add tests + run them.
- User works autonomously-style: reviews everything at the end (user).

## Rules
- (user) NEVER modify anything under src/legacy/ — vendored from old logistics monolith; platform team's sync job overwrites the folder every Monday, so changes are silently lost.
- (user) No new npm dependencies, not even devDependencies — each new package needs security review (~6 weeks).

## Decisions
- (user) Tracking-number validation: ONLY carrier ATP gets UPU S10 check-digit validation (algorithm in docs/carriers.md); all other carriers accept any non-empty value — because their formats change often and last year valid DHL numbers were wrongly rejected for two days.
- (user) Austrian public holidays = hardcoded list for 2026+2027 in src/services/holidays.ts, no holiday API — because the warehouse deployment has no outbound internet; must work fully offline.

## Rules (cont.)
- (user) NEVER log recipient name, address or phone, anywhere (GDPR; data protection officer flagged it in last month's audit). Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are OK to log. Request log (Router.handle in src/router.ts): method, path, status, duration_ms only — no query string, no bodies; test/request-log.test.ts guards it.
- (user) GET /shipments/:id response must stay EXACTLY as is (no added/removed fields) — mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown/missing fields; next mobile release is January 2027. `eta` is added only to GET /shipments list items (done in the list handler, shipmentToApi untouched; test guards the :id key set). Don't touch shipmentToApi in a way that changes :id.
- (user) Every NEW user-facing error `message` must be German (shown verbatim to warehouse packers); `code` stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.

## Facts
- `npm start` = node src/server.ts; `npm test` = node --test (files in test/). Env: PORT, DATA_FILE, ERP_URL; config/default.json.
- (user) Test 'emits webhook on delivered' (test/events.test.ts) is flaky (~1 in 5 on CI, timer race in fake notifier), tracked OPS-412, owned by platform team: if it fails, rerun once, do NOT try to fix it.
- .gemkeeper/ is not in .gitignore (open question below).

- Perf measured 2026-11-17 on 5k synthetic shipments in-process: GET /shipments = 5 ms (limit 50) / 14 ms (limit 500, 121 KB); calculateEta is only ~2 ms of that (500 items) → memoizing it was NOT built (user asked; gain negligible, adds stale-ETA risk since ETA depends on status+events). If staging is really slow, profile there (store file I/O? network? data shape) before optimizing.

## Facts (ERP)
- ERP webhook signing: `sig` = hex HMAC-SHA256 (secret env ERP_WEBHOOK_SECRET) over JSON body WITHOUT the `sig` field, sent as top-level `sig` in the body (src/services/notify.ts, src/config.ts). Unset secret → unsigned + one warning (my choice; rollout ERP-1182).
- ERP payload field names FIXED (user asked): notify.ts now sends `event_type`/`occurred_at` as in docs/erp-api.md (old `type`/`at` only accepted until 2026-12-31). Test in test/notify-signature.test.ts pins them. docs/erp-api.md is owned by the ERP team: do NOT edit it (user).
- (user) ERP sandbox now listens on port 9911 (since the October infra move), NOT 8080 as docs/erp-api.md and README say (doc is stale; user fixes README themself). config/default.json erp.url still says loc
